findings.description: The Lambda function embeds a static AWS access key ID and secret access key as plaintext environment variables in the Terraform source. These credentials are stored in state, visible to anyone with lambda:GetFunction or console read access, and can be exfiltrated by any code running in the function.

No kms_key_arn is specified, so the Lambda environment variables (which contain secrets here) are encrypted only with the default AWS-managed key, providing no customer-controlled key separation or access auditing for the sensitive values at rest.

No vpc_config block is defined, so the function runs outside any VPC with unrestricted outbound internet access and no security group or network ACL controls, easing data exfiltration if the function is compromised.
